import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers among clinical features
    clinical_features = [fid for fid, t in zip(feats.ids, feats.types) if t == 'clinical']
    
    # If no clinical features, try to find strong associations
    if not clinical_features:
        # Look for features with highest t-statistics
        t_stats = []
        for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
            if feats.types[i] != 'derived':
                # Compute Welch's t-test
                y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
                y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
                if len(y0) > 0 and len(y1) > 0:
                    t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
                    t_stats.append((abs(t_stat), fid))
        t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
        drivers = [fid for _, fid in t_stats[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
        return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Use clinical features as potential drivers
    drivers = tuple(clinical_features[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(clinical_features))])
    
    # Select features for logistic regression
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # For simplicity, select top features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] != 'derived':
            y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            if len(y0) > 0 and len(y1) > 0:
                t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
                t_stats.append((abs(t_stat), fid))
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top features excluding near-duplicates
    selected = set()
    for _, fid in t_stats:
        # Check if this feature is correlated with already selected ones
        is_duplicate = False
        for sel_fid in selected:
            col1 = feats.column(sel_fid)
            col2 = feats.column(fid)
            if col1 < feats.x.shape[1] and col2 < feats.x.shape[1]:
                corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1]
                if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                    is_duplicate = True
                    break
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected.add(fid)
            if len(selected) >= 10:  # Limit to reasonable number
                break
    
    # Create products for top features
    top_features = list(selected)[:5]
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            products.append((top_features[i], top_features[j]))
    
    columns = tuple(top_features)
    
    # Simple weighted loading based on effect size
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] != 'derived':
            y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
            y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
            if len(y0) > 0 and len(y1) > 0:
                t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
                loadings[fid] = abs(t_stat)
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
